manualTestLimitation: Browser-page inspection is unavailable under the computer-use restriction. Selecting the DeskPilot app also failed because the native computer-use connection closed. Synthetic tests are not presented as GUI or permission-grant verification.
namingScope: DeskPilot panel and menu names plus optional click-through badges on Mission Control thumbnails. The underlying Apple labels are unchanged.

nativeAccessibilityChecks.environment: Synthetic native accessibility tree; no live browser contents accessed
coverage: Application role is read before AXWindows to initialize Chromium native accessibility

resourceBehavior: Window routing remains event-based. Mission Control badges observe WindowManager and Dock with fallback checks every 1.5 seconds while idle and 0.25 seconds while visible. Disabling badges stops those checks.

chromeCatalogChecks.bookmarkTestContext: Synthetic files in a restricted test process. Minimal bookmarks passed; the sandbox rejected security-scope issuance, so the system file picker grant still needs GUI verification.
chromeCatalogChecks.liveFinding: The packaged GUI reported a denied Chrome catalog read. App-specific macOS logs also reported a code-requirement mismatch for SystemPolicyAppDataDetailed after development rebuilds. A later report came from an older app copy.
chromeCatalogChecks.liveReconnection: The user confirmed profile recognition in 0.2.3; its runtime reported a readable catalog with two profiles and later two recognized native Chrome windows out of three. This does not establish recognition of every window or post-upgrade permission.

codeSigning: Packaged build uses an ad hoc signature. An existing stable signing identity can be provided with DESKPILOT_SIGNING_IDENTITY for development. No privacy settings or signing certificates were changed.

liveWindowMovement.result: User confirmed moving one recognized Chrome profile to an existing desktop; its assignment was subsequently present in the application settings. The engine only saves that assignment after checking the native destination.
liveWindowMovement.automaticCreation: Not confirmed; the user reported that automatic creation and routing did not work.

missionControlDiscoveryChecks.environment: Synthetic accessibility trees and monitor geometry; no live Mission Control UI inspection
coverage: WindowManager-hosted mc.display is discovered even when Dock exposes an empty mc group
Older Dock-hosted hierarchy remains supported
An empty mc stub does not count as visible Mission Control and block routing
Native display IDs and unique full display geometry are matched
Conflicting or duplicate IDs, ambiguous geometry and partial trees are rejected

missionControlDiscoveryChecks.liveVerification: In 0.2.4, the packaged GUI reported WindowManager, desktop count increased from six to seven, assignment count increased from five to six, and the completed operation reported Done without an error. The user then reported that subsequent windows were not routed; this does not establish end-to-end automatic routing.

delayedWindowRegression.scenario: WindowServer lists a Chrome window before automation is enabled. Accessibility exposes it later on application activation, without a new window-created event. The previous engine skipped it; the corrected engine creates a desktop, confirms movement, and records its profile assignment.
delayedWindowRegression.environment: Real engine with a simulated system service
